title: Replace a plug-in control relay: seat it in its DIN-rail socket and snap the hold-down clip over it
instruction: Fit the new relay in the empty socket and latch its retaining clip.
context: Replacing a failed plug-in control relay is routine work for electricians and industrial maintenance workers (O*NET 47-2111.00 Electricians, 49-9071.00 Maintenance and Repair Workers, General; over 2 million US workers together). The relay's 14 blades have to go into the socket straight and all the way home, and the hold-down clip only closes over a relay that is fully seated; a relay left half in works loose with vibration.
setup: Millimetres; x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the robot's left, z above the table top; arm bases at y +305 and -305. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot. (1) A 200 x 160 x 5 mm steel control-panel back plate lying on the bench, 2 kg with its fittings, centred at x 300, y -100, carrying a 35 mm DIN rail (7.5 mm) along x and a black 14-pin relay socket, 70 x 29.5 mm, centred on the plate, its top face 37.5 mm above the bench with a 22 x 16 mm blade cavity 7 mm deep. (2) The socket's hold-down clip, a 44 x 24 mm hood with a catch lip, hinged on a post at the socket's +x end 74.5 mm above the bench; it starts open, leaning back on its stop 30 degrees past upright. (3) A new 4-pole plug-in relay, 21.5 x 28 x 36 mm body with its 14 blades (a 20 x 14 x 6.4 mm envelope) below, 35 g, standing upright in a black foam parts tray at x 200, y -245, blades in the tray's pocket, oriented the way the socket takes it.
scoring: Measured at the end of the trial. 0 for the rest of the trial if the back plate is pushed 5 mm on the bench or the relay is dropped (tipped over 60 degrees or off the bench). Otherwise: 1.0 (success, must hold for 1 s) when the relay sits flat on the socket (its body within 1 mm of the socket's top face, within 1.5 mm of the cavity's centre and 3 degrees of square) with the hold-down clip snapped under its catch, both grippers 30 mm or more from the relay, and nothing moving more than 1 mm for 1 s; 0.75 when it is seated and clipped but a gripper is near or something still moves; 0.5 when it is seated but the clip is not latched, with both grippers 30 mm or more from the relay; 0.25 when the blades went 2 mm into the socket at some point; else 0.
reset_notes: Open the clip back onto its stop, pull the relay straight up out of the socket and stand it back in the foam tray, blades in the pocket, coil terminals toward +x. Check the back plate is against its two bench stops.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at true size. The 14 blades are one 20 x 14 x 6.4 mm block in a 22 x 16 mm cavity; the contact springs are a plate in the cavity that holds until the blades push it with more than 3 N, then slides, and stays where it is pushed. The clip's catch is task code: pressed 1.5 degrees past flat it holds there. The back plate is loose and heavy.
